subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 21, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 21, 2026

Our development team has been busy polishing the welcome-screen experience with several commits addressing missing elements and visual consistency. Darren pushed fixes for persistent screen bugs in the fences utility, bringing version 1.0.2 to what should be full stability. These improvements ensure a smoother first-boot experience for new users installing our Arch-based distribution.

Natalie initialized the acreetionos-wallpapers repository with a fresh collection of artwork matching our emerald-black and neon-purple aesthetic. Meanwhile, the hydrogenos project gained a significant feature with local AI deployment via llama.cpp, including hardware detection for optimized inference. This work reflects our commitment to bringing privacy-respecting AI capabilities directly to the desktop.

On the infrastructure side, Darren continues refining the Calamares installer customization and GitLab CI pipelines that power our ISO builds. The build system improvements focus on reproducibility and faster turnaround for security updates. Our two-person team maintains full repository sovereignty while delivering a polished Arch experience without the typical suffering.

In broader community news, the LLVM project is wrapping up its relicensing effort, a significant milestone for the open-source compiler ecosystem. Vim Classic 8.3.1 has also been released, continuing the maintenance of the beloved editor's traditional codebase. These upstream developments directly benefit the toolchain underlying AcreetionOS.

Security updates from AlmaLinux arrived Friday covering bind9.18, bubblewrap, fence-agents, freerdp, grafana, and numerous other packages. We monitor these closely and integrate relevant patches into our rolling release schedule. Our commitment to rapid security response remains a top priority for the project.

Our Discord community at discord.gg/VHqQkJASw7 continues growing with active discussions about Cinnamon customization and Arch packaging. The team maintains presence on X, Bluesky, and Fosstodon for those preferring decentralized social platforms. Community feedback directly shapes our development road
